maria: Heads-up — getting pinged about TTFT and p99 for customer X. Can someone point me to the live panels and the shortest path to traces/logs? Need to paste into the async postmortem.

ben: Main landing is Grafana -> 'Latency / TTFT overview'. Panels to check: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, request rate, and the model heatmap. Quick link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/latency-ttft (open in prod). Jaeger traces: https://jaeger.redwood.ai (service=inference). Loki for logs: {app="inference", env="prod"} |~ "TTFT"

alex: Quick tip: when you're on the heatmap, click the cell for the model/timeslice then the little trace icon — it jumps straight to Jaeger with the right trace ID filters. Also the Grafana panel has a "View JSON" -> "Direct link" option to bookmark specific slices. @maria :eyes:

maria: thanks — is there a short PromQL I can paste for p95 (prod only) so the postmortem has an objective number?

ben: Use this (5m window):
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env="prod"}[5m])) by (le, model))
```
That returns p95 by model. Adjust window to 1m/10m if you need noisier/smoother.

sam: For tokens/sec the quick is:
```
sum(rate(inference_tokens_generated_total{env="prod"}[1m])) by (model)
```
If you want tokens per request: divide by rate(inference_request_count_total{env="prod"}[1m]).

maria: perfect. Who owns the grafana dashboard? I want to open a tiny PR to add a contextual note + link to the customer ticket.

alex: eng-infra owns the infra-facing dashboards; ping @ben for edits. For a PR: add the panel description (short note), add a dashboard-level link under "Links" to the customer ticket, and add one-sentence doc in the panel describing the preferred PromQL. Small changes generally get reviewed within 24h.

ben: I'll review the PR. For alert tuning — avoid noisy p99 alerts. Our recommendation: require sustained condition + minimum traffic for a slice. Example alert (pseudo):
```
# fire if slice had >200 requests in 5m AND p99 > 1.5s
(increase(inference_request_count_total{env="prod",slice="$SLICE"}[5m]) > 200)
  and (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env="prod",slice="$SLICE"}[5m])) by (le, model)) > 1.5)
```
Tune thresholds per-customer. Also add a suppression window (5m) and a runbook link.

maria: opening PR now and will tag @ben + @alex. I'll paste these PromQL snippets into the postmortem. Thanks all :thumbsup:
